ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The cell cycle is a series of events in the life of a dividing eukaryotic cell. It consists of four stages: G1, S, G2, and M. The duration of the cell cycle varies from one species to another and from one cell type to another. The G1 phase varies the most. For example, embryonic cells can pass through the G1 phase so quickly that it hardly exists, whereas neurons are arrested in the cell cycle and do not divide.
Mitosis occurs in all of the following types of cells EXCEPT

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a schematic diagram of the cell cycle; the circular cycle is labeled as the four phases G1, S, G2, and M, and the upper left clearly labels M as “mitosis”. The figure also shows G1 about 10 hours, S about 9 hours, and G2 about 4 hours. Reasoning: The question asks which type of cell does not undergo mitosis. According to the image and text, mitosis corresponds to the M phase in the cell cycle, which is the stage in which dividing eukaryotic cells replicate and allocate chromosomes. Mature red blood cells have no nucleus, so there are no intranuclear chromosomes to replicate and separate, and they cannot undergo mitosis. Therefore, the cell type that does not undergo mitosis is the red blood cell.

method.method_draft: From the image/text, identify mitosis as the M phase in the cell cycle of a dividing eukaryotic cell. Then use cell-structure knowledge: mature red blood cells do not have a nucleus, so they cannot replicate and segregate nuclear chromosomes in mitosis. Therefore the cell type that does not undergo mitosis is red blood cells.
